chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn al-Muzaffar al-Alawi al-Samarqandi narrated that Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ood, from his father, narrated that Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazal narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from al-Abbas ibn Hilal, said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) say:

Whoever fasts one day in Sha'ban seeking the reward of Allah will enter Paradise, and whoever seeks forgiveness seventy times each day in Sha'ban will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment in the company of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and honor from Allah will become due for him, and whoever gives charity in Sha'ban, even if it is half a date, Allah will forbid his body from the Fire, and whoever fasts three days in Sha'ban and connects them with the fasting of the month of Ramadan, Allah will record for him the fasting of two consecutive months.

key_terms.رَمَضَان: Ramadan, the ninth month of fasting
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban, the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for fasting and seeking forgiveness in the month of Sha'ban according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) highlights the month of Sha'ban as a period of spiritual preparation, linking these acts to the broader themes of repentance and anticipation of Ramadan. The emphasis on seventy daily supplications reflects the Shia tradition of consistent, high-volume dhikr to purify the soul before the fasting month. These rewards underscore the concept of 'connecting' (wasl) the spiritual momentum of Sha'ban with the obligatory fasts of Ramadan, ensuring a seamless transition into the month of divine mercy.
